issue_title: BSP_I2C1_Init calls the wrong MX_I2C1_Init function
clean_text:
Title: BSP_I2C1_Init calls the wrong MX_I2C1_Init function

Body:
### Overview

The BSP_I2C1_Init function in stm32h743i_eval_bus.c calls MX_I2C1_Init to initialize its I2C handle (hbus_i2c1). 

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ea644c0d-bec0-45dd-9160-f88ba8ede9f6)

stm32h743i_eval_bus.h declares a MX_I2C1_Init function with a weak modifier. The i2c.h peripheral initialization file generated by STM32CubeMX declares a MX_I2C1_Init function with no modifiers. During runtime, BSP_I2C1_Init calls the MX_I2C1_Init from i2c.c instead of stm32h743i_eval_bus.c meaning the I2C handle in stm32h743i_eval_bus.c doesn't actually get initialized. Any subsequent calls that route through stm32h743i_eval_bus.c to read from that I2C bus fail due to the I2C handle being uninitialized.

This confusing runtime behavior occurs because the linker is choosing the strong symbol over the weak symbol for any references to MX_I2C1_Init. You can prove this is a linker issue by removing the weak modifier from stm32h743i_eval_bus.h which causes a duplicate definitions linker error.

### Environment

This issue occurred while I was checking out the touchscreen of the STM32H753I-EVAL2 devkit. The EXC7200 touchscreen on that devkit utilizes I2C1 for communication. Calling BSP_TS_Init was returning the error code BSP_ERROR_COMPONENT_FAILURE due to a failure bubbled up from a called function. The called function routes through stm32h743i_eval_bus.c for I2C communication.

My project was setup using the board selector in STM32CubeMX 6.14.1 and selecting STM32H753I-EVAL2. I removed unused peripherals, but did not modify I2C1 from its default settings. The STM32CubeMX code generator was setup as follows:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a6e68dfb-1762-4fa2-8d52-2de39392c4ca)

After generating the IAR project:

1. Added the needed BSP files into the project
2. Modified main to simply call BSP_TS_Init
3. Built the application
4. Flashed and debugged on the target

### Fix

To workaround the issue I renamed the weak MX_I2C1_Init function declared in stm32h743i_eval_bus.h to something unique and updated references to MX_I2C1_Init in stm32h743i_eval_bus.c with the new name.

Am I using the BSP incorrectly or is there a bug in the BSP's implementation?

Title: LCD Reset bug disables Ethernet

Body:
STM32H743i_eval_lcd.c V3.3.1
The eval board does not have a reset line for the LCD device and if the reset function at line 242 is called it will try to use initialize and use PA2 as the reset line which is used by the RMII ethernet for MDIO.  This will prevent the ethernet phy from working correctly.
At the very least this line should be commented out.  Better still would be to remove the line and all code associated with initializing PA2 for use by the LCD which is found between lines 399 and 417.  It would also be good to remove all associated lines in the .h file for the defines used by the code so no one will question the relevance of an LCD reset.

Title: Wrong core

Body:
FreeRTOS examples are using the CM4F port.
<..>/Middlewares/Third_Party/FreeRTOS/Source/portable/RVDS/ARM_CM4F/port.c
Why don't they use the CM7 port?
<..>/Middlewares/Third_Party/FreeRTOS/Source/portable/RVDS/ARM_CM7/r0p1/port.c

Comments:
[HBOSTM - 2023-05-15T15:59:42Z]
Hello @carlo-dev-git ,

There are two options for running FreeRTOS on ARM Cortex-M7 microcontrollers.
The best option depends on the revision of the ARM Cortex-M7 core in use.
If the revision of the ARM Cortex-M7 core is not r0p1 then either option can be used, but it is recommended to use the FreeRTOS ARM Cortex-M4F port located in the /FreeRTOS/Source/portable/IAR/ARM_CM4F directory.

If the revision of the ARM Cortex-M7 core is r0p1 then use the FreeRTOS ARM Cortex-M7 r0p1 port located in the /FreeRTOS/Source/portable/IAR/ARM_CM7/r0p1 directory.

Best Regards,

[HBOSTM - 2023-06-14T16:24:51Z]
Hello @carlo-dev-git ,

Thank you for this contribution.
Please allow me to close this thread as answered. You may reopen it at anytime if you have any details to share with us in order to help you to solve the issue. Thank you for your comprehension.

With regards,

issue_title: stm32h74x eval BSP, stm32h743i_eval_sd.c, stm32h747i_eval_sd.c  - sd card detection BUG
clean_text:
Title: stm32h74x eval BSP, stm32h743i_eval_sd.c, stm32h747i_eval_sd.c  - sd card detection BUG

Body:
Setup:
Using STM32H743i-EVAL
Using STM32H743-FW-V1.11.0
file: stm32h743i_eval_sd.c, line 429
file: stm32h747i_eval_sd.c, line 434

BUG:
while calling the BSP_SD_DetectITConfig() function to set the edge detection for the SD card switch, the function always set the edge to rising regardless of the switch state.  This results in detecting  the card removal but never the card insertion.
The Bug is caused by improper use of "&&".  In this case it should be "&".
  
In both files, the statement should read:
 if(((uint32_t)BSP_IO_ReadPin(0, PinDetect[Instance]) & PinDetect[Instance]) != PinDetect[Instance])

Comments:
[HBOSTM - 2023-04-26T09:54:43Z]
Hello @OriginalGreenGuy,

Firstly, thank you for this contribution. There is no problem in the SD card demo on my side, however it is the BSP_SD_DetectCallback function that is responsible for detecting the presence of the SD card and not BSP_SD_DetectITConfig.
So, please allow me to close this issue and thank you again for your contribution.

Best Regards,
